issues.quote: the React design system used by the whole team
issues.problem: "Contributed" and "used by the whole team" hide what this person actually did. I can't tell if they built, owned or only patched the design system, so I can't judge their level or what they could own by day 30. In a pile of 120 frontend CVs, an unclear role on the headline achievement reads as a junior contribution.
issues.fix: Replace "Contributed" with a verb that shows ownership (built, led, maintained, introduced). Name what you personally shipped, such as components, design tokens or accessibility work. Add the scale: number of components, number of developers and projects using it.

issues.problem: Nothing in the CV shows testing, accessibility, Git workflow or CI/CD. A team lead needs those to know the candidate can ship reviewed, tested, accessible code without hand-holding. With no evidence of them, a five-year React/TypeScript profile looks like it covers building UI but not the engineering around it.
issues.fix: List only the tools actually used (for example Git, Jest or Testing Library, Cypress or Playwright, WCAG, CI). Show at least one in a bullet, such as test coverage on the design system or an accessibility audit fix, instead of leaving it as a bare skills line.

issues.problem: This is a Belgian CV, and "native" is not a CEFR level. English is the working language in most scale-up frontend teams, but its level is not stated. French is also missing a level. Employers here expect CEFR levels for all three languages.
issues.fix: Write all three on the CEFR scale in one line, for example "Dutch: C2 · English: C1 · French: B1" (use your real levels). Drop "native".

strength.quote: Improved the performance of the main web app
strength.why: Web performance work on the main product is the kind of user-visible, measurable result a team lead hires frontend people for. Once the before/after metric is filled in, this line shows ownership and impact and separates the candidate from applicants who only list frameworks.
